summary: ## **CENTRAL ELECTRICITY REGULATORY COMMISSION NEW DELHI** ## **Petition No: 259/MP/2026** **Coram:** **Shri Jishnu Barua, Chairperson Shri Ramesh Babu V., Member Shri Harish Dudani, Member Shri Ravinder Singh Dhillon, Member** **Date of Order: 19[th] June, 2026** ## **In the matter of:** Petition under Section 79 (1) (c) & (k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 42 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 seeking directions and/or guidelines for the implementation of Regulation 11A and Regulation 24.6, concerning nature and treatment of extensions or delayed commissioning by Renewable Energy Implementing Agencies (REIAs) or Distributions Licensees. ## **And in the matter of:** ## **Central Transmission Utility of India Limited** First Floor, Saudamini, Plot No. 2, Sector – 29, Near IFFCO Chowk Metro Station, Gurgaon, Haryana – 122001 ## **...Petitioner** ## **Vs.** ## **1. SJVN Limited** Order in Petition No. 259/MP/2026 **1** 6th Floor, Tower-1, Office Block, NBCC Complex, East Kidwai Nagar, New Delhi – 110023 ## ** Respondents** ## **Parties Present:** Shri Shubham Arya, Advocate, CTUIL Shri Aniket Prasoon, Advocate, APIPL ## **ORDER** The Petitioner, Central Transmission Utility of India Limited (‘CTUIL’), has filed the present Petition seeking necessary directions and/or guidelines in regard to the nature and treatment of extensions by Renewable Energy Implementation Agencies (REIAs) or distribution licensees for the purposes of compliance with Regulation 11A and Regulation 24 of the GNA Regulations, 2022. 2. The Petitioner has filed the present Petition seeking the following relief(s): _(a) Exercise its powers under Regulation 42 (Power to Remove Difficulties) of the GNA Regulations, 2022 to issue such directions or guidelines as may be necessary in regard to nature and treatment of the extensions by REIAs or Distribution Licensees for the purposes of compliance of Regulation 11A and Regulation 24 of the GNA Regulations, 2022;_ _(b) Issue directions/ clarification in regard to the extension granted to Azure by SECI and consequent exclusion of Azure from the Revocation List; and_ _(c) Pass such further order(s) or direction(s) as this Commission may deem just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case._ 3. The matter was heard on 3.6.2026. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed seeking necessary directions and/or guidelines in regard to the nature and treatment of extensions by Renewable Energy Implementation Agencies (REIAs) or distribution licensees for the purposes of compliance with Regulation 11A and Regulation 24 of the GNA Regulations. The learned counsel, while pointing out one such extension granted by Order in Petition No. 259/MP/2026 **2** SECI in the case of the Respondent No.1/APIPL, submitted that APIPL was granted Connectivity(ies) with a specified commissioning timeline of 30.9.2021, and the last date for compliance with Regulation 24.6 of GNA Regulations worked out as 31.12.2025. However, SECI _vide_ letter dated 9.1.2026 communicated the revised/ extended SCD for the awarded project capacity for which the PPAs were yet to be signed and requested that they be considered an extension of the SCD for the purposes of Regulation 24.6. However, in respect of 250 MW of awarded capacity, for which the SCD had been revised to 31.3.2028, a condition was imposed stating that the SCD considered the PSA/PPA signing by 31.3.2026. Based on the said letter from SECI, the Petitioner, as a matter of prudence, excluded APIPL’s name from the revocation list published on its portal on 20.1.2026 pertaining to non-compliance under Regulation 24.6 of GNA Regulations. However, since the extended SCD of 250 MW was stated to be contingent upon the signing of the PPA/PSA by 31.3.2026, CTUIL expressly reserved its right to seek necessary clarification or direction from the appropriate regulatory, adjudicatory or jurisdictional authority. The learned counsel further submitted that, as per CTUIL’s information, no PPA/PSA was signed by 31.3.2026, and CTUIL, therefore, on 1.6.2026, proceeded to revoke APIPL’s 250 MW Connectivity(ies)/deemed GNA and invoked the Connectivity Bank Guarantees furnished by it. The learned counsel also pointed out that subsequent to the filing of the present Petition, the Commission, in its recent order dated 31.5.2026 in Petition No. 1015/MP/2025 (Datta Power Infra Private Limited v CTUIL), has already clarified that the tentative SCOD, based on the tentative PPA that is yet to be signed, is not a valid document for the extension of SCOD, and thus, the issue raised in the present case stands addressed in terms thereof. 4. The matter was mentioned by the learned counsel for the Petitioner on 11.6.2026 and apprised that the Respondent, APIPL, is pursuing a separate Petition Order in Petition No. 259/MP/2026 **3** (Diary) No. 388/2026 along with IA (Diary) No. 389/2026, seeking quashing of the revocation of APIPL’s connectivity and other reliefs. Therefore, in terms of the order dated 31.5.2026 in Petition No. 1015/MP/2025 (Datta Power Infra Private Limited v CTUIL), nothing survives in the instant Petition. The learned counsel for the Petitioner sought permission to withdraw the instant Petition. The learned counsel for the Respondent, APIPL, did not oppose the Petitioner’s request for withdrawal of the Petition. 5. Considering the submissions of the learned counsels for the parties, the Petitioner is permitted to withdraw the present Petition. 6. Petition No. 259/MP/2026 is disposed of as withdrawn. **sd/sd/sd/sd/(Ravinder Singh Dhillon) (Harish Dudani) (Ramesh Babu V.)
